# Non-tail recursion

Tail recursion is when a function can directly return the result of a recursive call - there are no outstanding operations, and there is no need for the call stack frame to be preserved. So it can be translated to a ΓÇ£goto with argumentsΓÇ¥, and the stack usage will be constant.

In ΓÇ£non-tail recursionΓÇ¥, there are outstanding operations after the recursive call, and the stack frame cannot be nuked.
